rules.statement: Never disable warnings-as-errors (`TreatWarningsAsErrors=false`) in any project, tests and hosts included; relax a single rule with a justified `.editorconfig` entry or a narrowly scoped `#pragma`.
rules.why: Warnings-as-errors covers all code we maintain, not only code we ship.
rules.check: Diffs to project files or Directory.Build.props that set TreatWarningsAsErrors to false or add NoWarn broadly; a `#pragma warning disable` that covers more than the offending lines or has no justification.

rules.statement: Use `System.Text.Json` rather than `Newtonsoft.Json`, `JsonWebTokenHandler` rather than `JwtSecurityTokenHandler`/`JwtSecurityToken`, and never block on async code.
rules.why: These APIs are banned house-wide through BannedSymbols.txt (RS0030).
rules.check: References to Newtonsoft.Json, JwtSecurityTokenHandler, or `.Result` / `.Wait()` on tasks.

rules.statement: A change to an EF Core entity, entity type configuration or model contributor that changes a DbContext model must come with a new migration in the same change.
rules.why: Model drift that has no migration fails at runtime. The Definition of Done gate catches it before push.
rules.check: Entity or configuration edits in a diff that has no new migration files.

rules.statement: A migration only expands the schema (new tables, nullable or defaulted columns, indexes). It never drops, renames or tightens anything the previous release reads unless it is marked as a deliberate contract step, and raw SQL or seed-data changes must be classified as expand or contract.
rules.why: The previous release keeps serving while the migration runs and after a rollback. Making a column required or adding a unique index, constraint or foreign key to an existing table breaks it.
rules.check: A migration that drops or renames a column or table, makes a column non-nullable, or adds a unique, check, PK or FK constraint to an existing table without a contract marker; raw SQL or seed data with no expand/contract classification.

rules.statement: Remove the UTF-8 BOM from generated EF Core migration files, and revert a model snapshot whose only change is a BOM.
rules.why: Repository files are BOM-less (`charset = utf-8`), but `dotnet ef migrations add` writes BOMs and re-saves the snapshot even when nothing changed.
rules.check: New migration files that start with a BOM; snapshot files whose diff is only the BOM.

rules.statement: Put identifiers in double quotes inside hand-written SQL fragments in the EF model (`HasFilter`, `HasComputedColumnSql`, `HasDefaultValueSql`, and similar).
rules.why: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lower case, so a PascalCase column fails at runtime against Postgres even though SQLite tests and the drift gate pass.
rules.check: SQL string fragments in EF configuration that reference column or table names without escaped double quotes.

rules.statement: Keep hand-written code out of the `Migrations/` folder.
rules.why: `.editorconfig` treats `Migrations/` as generated code, so analyzers skip it.
rules.check: Non-generated helper classes or rules added under a Migrations folder.

rules.statement: Set package versions centrally in Directory.Packages.props, and never give a `PackageReference` an inline `Version`.
rules.why: The repository uses Central Package Management and lockstep versioning.
rules.check: `<PackageReference ... Version=` in project files.

rules.statement: Every CI workflow that builds or tests a .NET project checks out the full history (`fetch-depth: 0`).
rules.why: Nerdbank.GitVersioning computes the version from commit height, and the build fails on a shallow clone.
rules.check: An `actions/checkout` step without `fetch-depth: 0` in a workflow that builds or tests.

rules.statement: Keep functions small, doing one thing at a single level of abstraction, with at most 2–3 parameters. Turn a recurring group of parameters into a type. A trailing CancellationToken and a Try-pattern `out` don't count toward the limit.
rules.why: Clean Code: small, focused functions with few parameters are easier to read and test.
rules.check: Long, multi-purpose methods; methods with more than 3 data parameters; the same parameter group repeated across methods.

rules.statement: Follow Command–Query Separation: a method either performs an action or returns an answer, and a query never mutates state.
rules.why: Mixing the two hides side effects.
rules.check: Getter-like or query methods that also modify state.

rules.statement: When a caller needs a filtered subset of stored entities, call an intent-named store method that pushes the filter to the database and projects only the needed columns. Never page the whole set and filter in memory, and never expose `IQueryable`/`Expression` in the store contract.
rules.why: Filtering in the DBMS avoids loading every row, and the store contract stays ORM-agnostic.
rules.check: A `GetPageAsync` loop followed by in-memory filtering; `IQueryable` or `Expression` parameters in store interfaces.

rules.statement: Don't pass or return `null` where an empty or absent form exists, such as an empty collection.
rules.why: Null returns force null checks on every caller and invite NullReferenceExceptions.
rules.check: Methods returning null for collections, or null arguments where an empty value would do.

rules.statement: Use intention-revealing, searchable names, with no `Manager`/`Helper` catch-all names and no type encodings.
rules.why: Honest names make the code readable and searchable.
rules.check: New types named *Manager or *Helper; Hungarian-style prefixes.

rules.statement: Define a string literal used in more than one place (claim type, algorithm code, dictionary key) as a named `const` in one place, and give sentinel keys in shared dictionaries such as `HttpContext.Items` or `AuthenticationProperties.Items` a package prefix.
rules.why: Repeated literals drift apart, and unprefixed keys in shared dictionaries can collide.
rules.check: The same string literal in several places; un-namespaced keys written to HttpContext.Items or AuthenticationProperties.Items.

rules.statement: Report failures with typed exceptions that carry context rather than error codes, and never write an empty `catch` or an `async void` method.
rules.why: Empty catches swallow failures, and async void exceptions cannot be observed.
rules.check: `catch { }` blocks, `async void` methods, methods returning status codes for errors.

rules.statement: Write comments that explain why, not comments that restate what the code does, and never leave commented-out code.
rules.why: Git keeps the history, and restating comments add noise.
rules.check: Comments that paraphrase the code; blocks of commented-out code.

rules.statement: Model a concept that carries invariants as its own type rather than a bare `string`, `bool` or `int`.
rules.why: Primitive obsession spreads validation around and lets invalid values through.
rules.check: Bare primitives with implied invariants passed through many APIs.

rules.statement: Talk only to immediate collaborators, and avoid `a.B().C().D()` chains and feature envy.
rules.why: Law of Demeter: long chains couple code to distant structure.
rules.check: Long member-access chains that reach through several objects.

rules.statement: Never nest a function call inside another call's arguments. Assign the inner call's result to an intention-revealing local first.
rules.why: Each step is then named, debuggable and readable.
rules.check: Calls like `Process(GetValue(), ...)` with a method invocation as an argument.

rules.statement: Dispose every local `IDisposable`/`IAsyncDisposable` you own with a `using var` / `await using var` declaration rather than a nested block or try/finally, unless ownership is deliberately transferred. Never leave an `HttpResponseMessage`, `Stream` or factory-created HttpClient undisposed.
rules.why: Undisposed resources leak, and the declaration form is the house style.
rules.check: Disposable locals without `using`, `using (...) { }` blocks, or try/finally Dispose patterns.

rules.statement: Parse JSON into a detached `JsonElement` (`JsonElement.Parse`/`ParseValue`, or `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<JsonElement>` for streams), never into a `JsonDocument`.
rules.why: A JsonDocument rents pooled buffers that leak if it is not disposed, and elements read from it fail once it is disposed. JsonDocument parse APIs are banned.
rules.check: Calls to `JsonDocument.Parse`, `ParseAsync`, `ParseValue` or `TryParseValue`.

rules.statement: Name a parsed `JsonElement` for what it holds, or `jsonElement`, never `document`.
rules.why: `document` names a JsonDocument and misleads the reader.
rules.check: JsonElement variables named `document` or `doc`.

rules.statement: Read `JsonElement` members with the `NCode.Json` extension methods (`TryGetPropertyValue<T>`, `TryGetValue<T>`, `IsNullOrUndefined()`, `EmptyObject`/`OrEmptyObject()`) instead of hand-rolled `TryGetProperty` + `ValueKind` + `GetString()`/`GetInt64()` chains or re-parsing `"{}"`.
rules.why: The shared helpers convert by ValueKind and never throw, while the bare getters throw on a mismatched kind.
rules.check: Manual TryGetProperty/ValueKind/Get* chains, `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Null` checks, or parsing "{}".

rules.statement: Before reading members of JSON parsed from wire input, reject it unless `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object`.
rules.why: `JsonElement.TryGetProperty` throws InvalidOperationException on a non-object, so hostile input could fault the caller.
rules.check: Property reads on parsed request bodies or token headers/payloads without a prior object-kind check.

rules.statement: Parse a date/time string with `NCode.Json.DateCoercion` (`TryParseDateTimeOffset`/`TryParseDateTime`), never a hand-rolled `DateTime(Offset).TryParse`, and only when the value is declared to be a date. Never use it to guess whether an arbitrary string looks like a date.
rules.why: There is one invariant-culture date policy for all packages, and lenient sniffing would turn strings like "1.2" or "10:30" into dates.
rules.check: DateTime.TryParse or DateTimeOffset.TryParse calls; date parsing applied to untyped string values.

rules.statement: Read an RFC 7519 NumericDate strictly and with range guards through the NCode.Json helpers (`TryGetNumericDate`, `TryGetPropertyNumericDate`, `DateCoercion.TryParseNumericDate`/`TryFromNumericDate`), never through `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds`/`FromUnixTimeMilliseconds`.
rules.why: The BCL methods throw on out-of-range input, so wire input could fault the caller.
rules.check: FromUnixTimeSeconds/Milliseconds calls; NumericDate read from a JSON string.

rules.statement: Treat a time claim that is present but invalid as a validation failure, never as an absent claim, and saturate or compare elapsed time instead of adding a margin that can overflow near `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue`.
rules.why: Reading a malformed claim as absent weakens validation, and margin arithmetic can overflow.
rules.check: Code that ignores an unparseable exp/nbf/iat; `instant + skew` additions without saturation.

rules.statement: Read a count of seconds sent by a remote party (`expires_in`, `interval`) with `TryGetWholeInt32`/`TryGetPropertyWholeInt32` or `WholeInt32JsonConverter`, never `JsonElement.TryGetInt32` or the serializer's default int handling.
rules.why: Peers may write whole numbers as `60.0` or `6e1`, which the BCL readers reject.
rules.check: TryGetInt32 or plain int-typed serialized members for peer-sent second counts.

rules.statement: Stamp instants that a JWT or stored grant carries with NCode.Time's whole-second helpers (`GetUtcNowWithPrecisionInSeconds()`, `GetTimestampWithPrecisionInSeconds()`, `WithPrecisionInSeconds()`).
rules.why: A stored time must equal the NumericDate it round-trips through.
rules.check: `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()` used for token or grant timestamps without truncation to whole seconds.

rules.statement: Never put a helper with a method body in an `*.Abstractions` package.
rules.why: Abstractions packages stay contract-only, and general helpers live in dependency-free packages.
rules.check: Classes with implementation code added to *.Abstractions projects.

rules.statement: Cap the lifetime of a client-supplied JWT through the validator's lifetime requirement (a max-lifetime option), never with ad-hoc `exp` arithmetic, and keep its replay record until `exp` plus the effective clock skew.
rules.why: The lifetime requirement measures from the earliest asserted iat/nbf, so the client cannot game it.
rules.check: Manual comparisons of exp against now plus a constant; replay retention set with a fixed margin.

rules.statement: Validate a received JWT with an explicit algorithm allow-list for signature, key management, content encryption and compression, where an unset list permits nothing, and with decryption keys named explicitly as the recipient's. Never re-check `alg` by hand after validation in place of the allow-list.
rules.why: A check after decoding runs after the cryptography it must precede, and unset-means-all opens algorithm confusion.
rules.check: Validation without allowed-algorithm lists; unset settings treated as permit-all; post-validation alg checks; signer keys used for decryption.

rules.statement: Branch on why validation failed using the machine-readable failure code, never the message text.
rules.why: Message text is not a stable contract.
rules.check: String matching on exception or failure messages.

rules.statement: Sign and encrypt a JWT addressed to a client with the algorithms and public keys the client registered. Fail with `server_error` rather than substitute an algorithm, never take the first listed algorithm, never encrypt to a shared or tenant key, and never compress a server-produced JWT.
rules.why: The client's registered metadata governs, and RFC 8725 §3.6 forbids compression.
rules.check: Picking algorithms[0]; tenant keys used for client encryption; a `zip` header set on produced tokens.

rules.statement: Write a key embedded in a JOSE header (`epk`, DPoP `jwk`) with only its public members, and refuse a received one that carries private members.
rules.why: Anyone holding the token can read the header, so a private member there discloses key material.
rules.check: Header keys serialized with private parameters (d, p, q, etc.); tests reading private members from produced tokens.

rules.statement: Take a client's public keys from a single source (stored keys or `jwks_uri`, never both), import them under one policy (public only, consistent `use`/`key_ops`/`alg`, unique `kid`), and never use a `kid` as a globally unique secret identifier.
rules.why: A kid is the owner's name for a key, not a unique identifier, and every entry point must enforce the same import policy.
rules.check: Merging stored keys with jwks_uri keys; imports that skip the policy checks; a kid used as a storage id.

rules.statement: Read a client certificate through one resolver that trusts only the configured forwarded header behind a proxy, never `HttpContext.Connection.ClientCertificate` or the header directly, and treat an undecodable forwarded value as `invalid_request`, never as an absent certificate.
rules.why: Behind a proxy the connection certificate belongs to the proxy, and a malformed credential must fail visibly.
rules.check: Direct reads of Connection.ClientCertificate or certificate headers; decode failures treated as no certificate.

rules.statement: Give a typed `Claim` its value in the declared type's XML Schema lexical form, formatting numbers with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`.
rules.why: A culture-formatted value such as "1,000" does not parse strictly as its declared type.
rules.check: Claim values built with ToString() without InvariantCulture.

rules.statement: Prefer instance members behind an interface, registered as a DI singleton, over static utility classes, and never keep static mutable or ambient state.
rules.why: A singleton performs like a static and stays mockable, while static state hurts testability.
rules.check: New static classes with logic that has dependencies; mutable static fields.

rules.statement: Never store a captured `HttpContext`, request-scoped `IServiceProvider` or `ClaimsPrincipal` in a field or property. Use a live view over `IHttpContextAccessor`, or take the dependency as a method parameter.
rules.why: Captured request state goes stale and causes use-after-request bugs.
rules.check: Fields or properties holding HttpContext, scoped providers or principals.

rules.statement: Constructor-inject every dependency, with no `new` of collaborators and no service location. The exception is a singleton resolving scoped or generically selected services at the point of use, and a closed set of singletons is injected as `IEnumerable<T>`.
rules.why: Injected dependencies keep the code testable.
rules.check: `new` of service collaborators inside methods; GetService calls where injection was possible.

rules.statement: Wrap dependencies that can't be mocked (clock, `Guid.NewGuid()`, crypto RNG, `Activity`) in a thin internal interface facade with an internal sealed forwarding implementation marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, registered in DI.
rules.why: Callers become unit-testable by mocking the facade.
rules.check: Direct `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, `Guid.NewGuid()` or RNG calls in production logic.

rules.statement: Use `internal virtual` for one-off override seams, leave internal implementation classes unsealed for mocking, and never make public members `virtual` just for testability. Mock the interface instead.
rules.why: A public virtual member is a permanent SemVer-bound override point that a subclass can use to weaken security controls.
rules.check: New `public virtual` members added for tests; sealed internal implementations that tests need to mock.

rules.statement: Expose internals to tests through `InternalsVisibleTo` (plus `DynamicProxyGenAssembly2`), and never widen the public surface for tests.
rules.why: Test-only access stays internal.
rules.check: Members made public solely for tests.

rules.statement: Test units through their public surface rather than private methods. Delete private branches the tests can't reach, or extract complex privates into a collaborator.
rules.why: Private methods are not seams, and an unreachable branch is dead code.
rules.check: Reflection used to call privates; unreachable private branches.

rules.statement: Every type or member is either covered by tests or annotated `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, and only thin passthroughs, DI wiring and framework adapters are excluded.
rules.why: Code with behavior must be tested.
rules.check: New untested behavioral code; ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on code with logic.

rules.statement: Record consumer-visible changes in CHANGELOG.md under `## [Unreleased]`.
rules.why: Consumers rely on the changelog to see what changed.
rules.check: PRs that change public behavior or surface without a changelog entry.
